title: Cyrus and the Escarpment
premise: Emrys Yarrow, a railroad engineer who has spent fifteen years mapping closed lines to stay off the world's radar, is pulled back into service when an upriver survey expedition goes silent. Following their route into the Escarpment, he finds the team alive but changed—they've uncovered a pre-railroad tunnel network that proves the government's founding settlement was built on a buried massacre, a truth worth killing for. Emrys must choose between the duty he owes the expedition's sponsor and the love he rekindles with its cartographer, Sera Voss, who wants the finding published. In the end, Emrys burns his own map and lets the expedition's evidence go downriver with Sera while he stays behind to hold the line—surviving, but at the cost of the invisibility that once kept him safe.
about_author: Dominic Ravensworth is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years on remote rail crews before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who measure the world in distances they'd rather not cross.

chapters.title: The Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Emrys Yarrow's POV. Fifteen years after walking away from the government survey corps, Emrys lives quietly as a railroad engineer, obsessively mapping decommissioned lines no one will ever ride. A telegram arrives: the Meridian Expedition upriver has missed three scheduled radio checks, and the sponsor wants him specifically. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility cracking under an old debt.

chapters.title: What the Sponsor Knows
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the port city of Callow's Reach, Emrys meets Aldous Crane, the expedition's wealthy sponsor, who offers triple pay and a sealed envelope of instructions Emrys is forbidden to open until he finds the camp. Emrys recognizes the handwriting on the envelope—it belongs to Sera Voss, the woman he left fifteen years ago. Emotional beat: suspicion braided with longing.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with interludes from Sera's recovered journal. Emrys hires a boat and follows the expedition's route through narrowing gorges, finding abandoned supply caches cut open from the inside. The journal entries grow stranger, describing tunnels beneath the river that appear on no map—including one of Emrys's own closed lines. Emotional beat: dread mounting as geography stops making sense.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Camp
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. Flashback to the expedition's discovery: a vast tunnel system beneath the escarpment containing bones, colonial-era shackles, and documents proving the founding settlement exterminated the laborers who built it. The team voted to go public; two members sided with Crane's man, Rennick, who wants it buried. Emotional beat: idealism curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Silence on the Radio
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys reaches the camp and finds it half-ruined, the radio smashed, four survivors hiding in the tunnels: Sera, her brother Tomas, the geologist Okonkwo, and a wounded Rennick they can't trust. The others are dead or gone over the escarpment with the evidence crates. Emotional beat: reunion shadowed by grief and mutual accusation.

chapters.title: Rennick's Bargain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Rennick reveals Crane's orders: recover or destroy every document, and kill anyone who resists. He offers Emrys his old life back—full reinstatement, the closed lines reopened—in exchange for Sera's silence. Emrys stalls, buying time by claiming he knows a rail spur out of the escarpment that Rennick's maps don't show. Emotional beat: duty and desire pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Spur
chapters.summary: Tomas Voss's POV. The group moves through the tunnels toward Emrys's secret spur line, pursued by Rennick's men who arrived by river. Okonkwo sacrifices himself collapsing a passage to buy hours, and Tomas learns why Emrys vanished fifteen years ago: he refused to falsify a survey that would have condemned a valley town. Emotional beat: grudging respect becoming trust.

chapters.title: Crane Arrives
chapters.summary: Aldous Crane's POV. Crane himself comes upriver with armed men and a magistrate's writ declaring the expedition lost, its records state property. He confronts Emrys with the truth of their shared past—Crane covered for Emrys's refusal years ago and considers the debt paid. Emotional beat: the patron unmasked as the architect of everything Emrys fled.

chapters.title: The Last Mile
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax. On the crumbling spur above the gorge, Emrys runs a hand-car loaded with the evidence while Sera holds Rennick's men at the tunnel mouth. Rennick falls; Crane, exposed on the trestle as Emrys cuts the line behind him, chooses the evidence over rescue and is lost with it—but Sera memorized the documents, and Tomas carries copies sewn into his coat. Emotional beat: survival purchased with irreversible loss.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, then Emrys's. Weeks later, the story breaks in the coastal papers; Crane's empire unravels posthumously. Sera publishes under the expedition's name, honoring the dead, and comes looking for Emrys—not to pull him back into the world, but to walk a closed line beside him. Emrys burns his old maps. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid, and love chosen without surrendering either self.
